text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro arrives for a two-day official visit to Estonia today.

- A public opinion poll shows that the voters would still prefer the Reform Party (support 13 percent) followed by the Centre Party (10 percent). The Coalition Party would receive 6 percent of ballots cast if an election were held now.
- Economy Minister Jaak Leimann rejects claims that the cooperation agreement with the Russian Orenburg region harms Estonia's interests.
- The amended law on education enables students to apply to anmy bank they want for a student loan. Savings Bank is the only bank which currently is allowed to grant student or study loans.

- The planned meeting of five presidents in Tallinn next week was a joint idea of Ukraine and Estonia, the presidential office announced. The presidents of the three Baltic states, Ukraine and Poland will meet on Tuesday.
- Two Estonian computer firms, Microlink and Astrodata, were selected as the suppliers of hardware for Estonia's schools. Most of the computers will be set up in Tallinn.
- The five-day theatre festival Dionysia '97 began in Tartu on Wednesday.
- The Estonian Shipping Co received the fifth container carrier from the Dutch shipyard Bijholt B.V. on Tuesday. The ship was named "Kurkse".
- Nordic business newspaper plan to establish a new English-language business paper to cover the Baltic Sea region.
